name: geochemical_world
description: og-00's real serpentinizing vent (genuine PHREEQC peridotite speciation feeding a genuine FiPy finite-volume advection-diffusion solve) rebuilt as the Phase-1 geochemical world: both mechanisms are selected through typed faces (model_serpentinization: phreeqc | reduced; model_spatial_transport: fipy convecting | fipy_uniform_upflow | fenics), so the model CLASS is a categorical sweep axis beside the physical parameters, and a ConservationLedgerProcess audits integrated sources against accumulated pools, charge balance, flux divergence and heat directionality (ledger/ledger_ok). The free parameters are the vg-data package 'vent_environment' (value-or-distribution, units, context, source, provenance class), which the environmental-calibration ensemble samples.

model_serpentinization.description: Model class behind the 'serpentinization' face: phreeqc | reduced

model_spatial_transport.description: Model class behind the 'spatial_transport' face: fenics | fipy | fipy_uniform_upflow

flow_velocity.description: Boundary water flux through the reaction zone (m/s) [vg-data: inferred]

olivine_rate.description: Olivine reaction extent per flow-saturated step [vg-data: hypothetical]

pyroxene_fraction.description: Diopside per mole olivine (peridotite vs dunite) [vg-data: calibrated]

fe_fraction.description: Fayalite fraction of the dissolving olivine [vg-data: extrapolated]

heat_to_fluid_fraction.description: Serpentinization enthalpy retained in the fluid [vg-data: calibrated]

nx.description: FiPy finite-volume cells across the interface column

serpentinization.doc:
Real PHREEQC serpentinization source: ``(T, flow, DIC) -> H2 / alkalinity / heat``.

Drives the genuine IPhreeqc engine every step. Emits the serpentinization
*source* into the vent fluid as composable ``float`` deltas (H2, alkalinity,
heat accumulate; a sibling transport process removes them by advection, so
the vent fluid settles at source = sink), plus ``overwrite[float]`` sensor
readings (instantaneous fluxes, pe, and the PHREEQC charge imbalance that
the ``charge_neutrality`` invariant audits).

_contract.summary: Real PHREEQC serpentinization source: (T, flow, DIC) -> H2, alkalinity, heat.
_contract.description: Drives the genuine USGS IPhreeqc engine every step over a peridotite assemblage (forsterite + fayalite + diopside with serpentine / brucite / magnetite / quartz). Emits the serpentinization source into the vent fluid as additive float deltas (H2, alkalinity, heat accumulate; a sibling transport process removes them, so the fluid settles at source = sink), plus overwrite sensors: instantaneous fluxes, redox pe, the equilibrium pH, and the PHREEQC charge imbalance the charge_neutrality invariant audits.

inputs.DIC: dissolved inorganic carbon fed back from the vent fluid (molar)

outputs.H2: dissolved H2 source delta (molar) - reducing power

math: H2 arises from Fe(II) -> Fe(III) oxidation by water; PHREEQC solves the full multicomponent speciation
source flux_i  ~  olivine_rate * fe_fraction * window(T),   window(T) = exp(-((T - t_opt)/t_width)^2)

symbols.olivine_rate: prescribed olivine dissolution rate (per flow-saturated reaction progress)
symbols.fe_fraction: Fe-olivine (fayalite) fraction — the Fe(II) oxidised to magnetite + H2
symbols.pyroxene_fraction: diopside dissolved per olivine (makes it peridotite -> Lost City Ca-OH pH)

assumptions: Partial equilibrium: a prescribed olivine dissolution rate feeds full PHREEQC speciation each step.
Peridotite (olivine + diopside), not dunite, so Ca-OH buffering reaches the Lost City high-pH endmember.

transport.doc:
Real 2-D FiPy advection–diffusion–reaction vent–ocean cross-section.

Reads the serpentinization drivers (``H2``/``alkalinity``/``heat``) plus the
current interface ``temperature``/``pH``/``porosity`` and the boundary
``flow_velocity``, solves a 2-D heat + solute field across the wall (cold
ocean left, source entering at the base, buoyant upflow, vent exit at the
top) with the genuine FiPy FVM solver, and emits first-order **deltas** (bare
``float``, composable) that move the outlet T/pH toward the vent-exit field
and shrink porosity as precipitation clogs the pores. The normalised max FVM
balance residual is published as an ``overwrite[float]`` sensor
(``flux_divergence_residual``) proving spatial flux conservation.

_contract.summary: Real 2-D FiPy advection-diffusion-reaction vent-ocean cross-section: transports the serpentinization source across the interface and up the chimney.
_contract.description: Reads the serpentinization drivers (H2 / alkalinity / heat) and the current interface temperature / pH / porosity plus the boundary flow, solves a 2-D heat and solute field with the genuine FiPy finite-volume solver (TransientTerm == DiffusionTerm - PowerLawConvectionTerm under buoyant upflow, scipy LinearLUSolver): cold acidic ocean on the left face, the serpentinizing source entering at the base, vent fluid rising and exiting at the top. Emits first-order additive deltas that move the outlet T / pH toward the vent-exit field and shrink porosity as precipitation clogs the pores, plus the normalised max FVM balance residual as an overwrite sensor witnessing spatial_flux_conservation to the solver tolerance. The full 2-D fields are the real cross-section the campaign visualization renders.

outputs.temperature: temperature delta toward the vent-exit field (K)
outputs.pH: pH delta toward the vent-exit field (dimensionless)
outputs.flux_divergence_residual: normalised max FVM balance residual (dimensionless, ~machine eps)

math: dc/dt = div(D grad c) - div(u c) + R        (advection-diffusion-reaction)
FiPy form: TransientTerm == DiffusionTerm - PowerLawConvectionTerm, scipy LinearLUSolver
flux_divergence_residual = max |div(flux)| / scale  (spatial flux conservation witness)
assumptions: 2-D porous-wall cross-section with prescribed boundary fluxes (ocean left, source base, vent exit top).
Buoyant upflow carries the source up the chimney; lateral diffusion mixes with the cold ocean.
pH and porosity fields are derived from the real transported solute field (ocean<->vent mixing).

conservation_ledger.doc: Integrate published source rates and audit them against the accumulated pools.

_contract.summary: Conservation ledger: integrates source rates and audits pools, charge, flux and energy directionality.
_contract.description: Every tick, integrates the H2 / alkalinity / heat source rates the serpentinization class publishes and compares the running integral with the pools the composite accumulated (the matter + energy ledger — exact by construction when every process writes additive deltas to the same store). Tracks the worst-case PHREEQC charge imbalance and the FVM flux divergence residual, and a directionality witness (serpentinization heat is released, never absorbed). ledger_ok = 1 when every residual is below the configured tolerance.

outputs.H2_in: integrated H2 source (same units as the pool)
outputs.energy_directionality: 1 if the heat source has never been negative, else 0
outputs.ledger_ok: 1 if every residual is within tolerance, else 0

assumptions: Every process writing the audited pools returns additive deltas (bare float), so the pool equals the running integral of the published rates.
The ledger runs at the same interval as the source process, so it reads each published rate exactly once.

emitter.doc:
Store historical states in memory.

``subsample`` records only every Nth composite tick (default 1 =
every tick). Use this for long runs or composites with heavy
state (large fields, many agents) to keep RAM bounded — the
saved time-series still reflects the simulation's true cadence
via each row's ``global_time`` field.

``max_len`` optionally bounds ``history`` to the most recent N
recorded rows (a ring buffer): once the cap is reached each new
record drops the oldest. Default ``None`` = unbounded (the
historical behaviour — consumers such as v2ecoli that read the
full ``history`` are unaffected unless they opt in). ``max_len``
counts *recorded* rows (i.e. post-``subsample``).
